rows.question: How do I change the address on my driving licence?
keyFacts: It does not cost anything to change your address with DVLA
You can apply online (or by post)

answer.answer: Update your address online at GOV.UK. The service is free and you'll need your driving licence number and National Insurance number. You must tell DVLA when your address changes, and a new photocard licence is posted to your new address. You can keep driving while you wait for it. Failing to update can lead to a fine of up to £1,000.

rows.question: How much does it cost to renew my driving licence when I turn 70?
keyFacts: Renewing your driving licence at 70 or over is free

answer.answer: It's free. When you turn 70, your photocard licence is valid until you reach 70, and you then renew it for free, and free again every 3 years after that. A replacement licence (for example, if yours is lost or damaged) costs £14.

rows.question: How old do I have to be to apply for a provisional driving licence?
keyFacts: You must be at least 15 years and 9 months old
It costs £34 to apply online

answer.answer: You can apply for a provisional car licence (category B) from 15 years and 9 months old, and for a moped (category AM) from 15 years and 6 months. You must be 17 to drive a car on public roads, or 16 if you receive the higher rate mobility component of Disability Living Allowance.

rows.question: How much does it cost to replace a stolen driving licence?
keyFacts: A replacement licence costs £20 online

answer.answer: It costs £14 to replace a stolen photocard driving licence in the UK when you apply on GOV.UK. Replacing a licence is not free in this case, but changing your name or address on it is.

rows.question: How long do penalty points stay on my licence?
keyFacts: Penalty points/endorsements stay on your driving record for 4 or 11 years, depending on the offence

answer.answer: Most penalty points stay on your licence for 4 years from the date of the offence. Drink or drug driving convictions stay for 11 years.

rows.question: How much does the car theory test cost?
keyFacts: The car theory test costs £23

answer.answer: The UK car (Category B) theory test costs £23. This fee is payable when you book, and it is the same for the standard test in Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

rows.question: How do I tell DVLA my car is off the road?
keyFacts: Tell DVLA online (or by phone/post) that the vehicle is off the road: a SORN
You get a refund for any full months of remaining tax

answer.answer: Make a Statutory Off Road Notification (SORN) online at gov.uk, which is free. You need the vehicle's registration number and details from its V5C logbook. You can also post the SORN declaration from the V5C logbook to DVLA. Once SORN is made, the car must not be driven or parked on a public road, though it can stay on private land. If it was taxed, you can claim a refund for full remaining months. You must tax it again before using it on a public road.

rows.question: Can I get a refund on my vehicle tax if I sell my car?
keyFacts: You cancel vehicle tax by telling DVLA you no longer have the vehicle (for example sold, scrapped or off the road); there is no other way
You get a refund for any full months of remaining tax

answer.answer: Yes. If you sell or transfer the car, tell DVLA and cancel its vehicle tax to get a refund for each full month left on the tax. You can't get a refund for the part-month. You must tell DVLA, either online or by post, and the refund is not paid automatically. You can't drive the car untaxed in the meantime, so the new keeper needs to tax it before it's used on the road.

rows.question: Which vehicles are exempt from vehicle tax?
keyFacts: Historic vehicles built before 1 January 1986 are exempt from vehicle tax
Vehicles used by a disabled person can be exempt
Electric cars are no longer exempt: from 1 April 2025 they must pay vehicle tax

answer.answer: Common VED (vehicle tax) exemptions include: vehicles registered as disabled (for example, with a Motability or Blue Badge-linked entitlement, or where the registered keeper receives qualifying disability benefits); historic vehicles built more than 40 years ago, which are taxed under a free historic vehicle tax class; certain agricultural and forestry vehicles and machinery, such as tractors and road rollers; and some public service vehicles, such as fire engines and ambulances. Eligibility depends on the exact vehicle type and keeper, and zero-emission electric cars have had changes to their VED rules from April 2025, so check the current rules before assuming an exemption.

You get a refund for any full months of vehicle tax left

rows.question: What are the penalties for speeding?
keyFacts: The minimum penalty is a £100 fine and 3 penalty points
You could be disqualified if you reach 12 or more points within 3 years

answer.answer: For most speeding offences the usual penalty is a £100 fixed penalty notice and 3 penalty points on your licence. Courts can impose a fine based on weekly income (up to £2,500 for some offences), plus points or disqualification. You can be disqualified for at least 6 months if you reach 12 points within 3 years (totting up), or immediately for very serious speeding (for example, 100 mph or more). Drivers who passed their test within the last 2 years lose their licence if they reach 6 points. In some areas you may be offered a speed awareness course instead of points, but only if you have not taken one in the last 3 years.

rows.question: What are the eyesight rules for driving?
keyFacts: You must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres away
Minimum visual acuity of decimal 0.5 (6/12) on the Snellen scale, with glasses or contact lenses if needed

answer.answer: You must be able to read a vehicle number plate from 20 metres away, using glasses or contact lenses if you need them. Your visual field must also meet the standard (at least 120 degrees horizontally, with no significant defect in the central 20 degrees). You must tell the DVLA if your eyesight doesn't meet the standard in either eye, or if you have a condition that affects your vision. You must not drive if you don't meet the standard.

rows.question: How do I change the photo on my driving licence?
keyFacts: It costs £14 to change the photo online
You do this by renewing your licence (online, or by post for £17)

answer.answer: Apply for a replacement photocard licence on GOV.UK. Use the online service, upload a new photo that meets the passport-style requirements, and pay the replacement fee (currently £20). Your old licence stays valid until the new one arrives, and you should destroy the old one once you receive it. Check the GOV.UK page for the current fee and photo rules before applying.

rows.question: What do the codes on my driving licence mean?
keyFacts: The codes on the back of the licence set conditions you must meet to drive
Examples: 01 eyesight correction (glasses or contact lenses); 78 automatic transmission only

answer.answer: Your photocard licence shows two kinds of codes. Section 10 lists the vehicle categories you're entitled to drive, such as B (cars up to 3,500kg and 8 passengers plus the driver), B1, C1, and so on. Section 12 lists restriction codes, which set conditions on your licence. Common examples are 01 (must wear glasses or contact lenses), 78 (automatic vehicles only) and 79 (vehicle adapted for a disability, with a sub-code describing the adaptation). Check the full list on GOV.UK for any code you don't recognise.

rows.question: How do I swap my paper driving licence for a photocard?
keyFacts: You do not need to exchange a valid paper licence unless you change your address or name, want to do Driver CPC training, or it is damaged, lost or stolen
It is free if you changed your name or address and still have the paper licence
Otherwise a new photocard licence costs £20

answer.answer: Apply online at GOV.UK for a photocard licence, choosing the option to exchange your paper licence. You'll need a digital passport-style photo, your National Insurance number, and your current paper licence details. The exchange is free. Your paper licence stays valid until you receive the photocard, and you should destroy the old paper licence once the new one arrives. You can also apply by post using form D1, but online is quicker.

rows.question: How much does the driving test cost?

It costs £75 on evenings, weekends and bank holidays

rows.question: How do I change my driving test appointment?

rows.question: How do I tax a car if I haven't received a tax reminder?
keyFacts: You can tax online with the 11-digit reference number from your V5C (or the 12-digit number on the green new keeper slip)
You can also tax by phone or at a Post Office

answer.answer: You don't need the reminder letter. Go to GOV.UK, enter the vehicle's registration number, and pay the Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) online. You'll need a valid insurance policy (DVLA checks the Motor Insurance Database) and a valid MOT if the car needs one. Not receiving a reminder doesn't excuse you from taxing the vehicle. If you're not using the car on public roads, make a SORN (Statutory Off Road Notification) instead.

You also need valid insurance, and an MOT if the car is over 3 years old. Vehicle tax can be paid from the date you buy the car, and the DVLA will then send you a new V5C in your name, usually within a few weeks.

rows.question: Will my appeal against a speeding fine succeed?

rows.question: How much income tax will I pay on a company car?

answer.answer: You pay income tax on a company car as a benefit in kind. The taxable amount is the car's P11D list price (including extras, minus any employee contributions) multiplied by a percentage set by its CO2 emissions (or, for electric cars, its zero-emission range). For 2025/26, electric cars are 3% of list price, rising to 4% in 2026/27 and 5% in 2027/28. Petrol and diesel cars are charged at higher percentages depending on CO2 band. You then pay income tax on that amount at your usual rate (20%, 40% or 45%). Example: a £30,000 electric car at 3% gives a £900 taxable benefit, so a 40% taxpayer pays £360 a year. Your employer also pays Class 1A National Insurance on the benefit.
